prompt: From /data/products.json, give me a list that keeps only the 'id' and 'name' fields of each product. Report the result in prose.

function.name: parse_json
function.description: Parse a JSON string and return the resulting value (object, array, or scalar). Throws on invalid JSON.

function.name: extract_field
function.description: Read a JSON value at the given absolute file path and return the value at the given JSONPath expression, e.g. "$['users'][?(@.id==42)].email". Returns null if no node matches.

function.name: transform_json
function.description: Apply a small set of named transforms to a JSON value loaded from disk. Returns the transformed value as a JSON string. `operation` is one of: 'rename_field' (rename a top-level field — args: {"from": "old_name", "to": "new_name"}), 'drop_field' (remove a top-level field — args: {"field": "field_name"}), 'project' (keep only a whitelisted set of top-level fields — args: {"fields": ["field_a", "field_b"]}).

function.name: filter_records
function.description: Load a JSON file containing a list of records (or an object with a 'records' field), apply a JSONPath predicate filter, and return the matching records as a JSON array. Returns an empty array if nothing matches.

path.description: Absolute path to a JSON file on disk containing a list (or {records: [...]})
